whatTheyArgued: The Physiology of Taste (1825; Robinson 1854 English, read on disk from Gutenberg) is a miscellany: twenty aphorisms, thirty 'meditations' on taste, appetite, digestion and other topics, and anecdotes. It is not a sampling or rejection method. Its nearest relevant claims: aphorism XIII, that never changing one's drinks is a heresy because the tongue saturates and after the third glass gives an obtuse sensation; XI-XII on ordering food from substantial to light and drink from mild to foamy; VIII that at table ennui does not strike for the first hour; and IX that a new dish does humanity more good than a new star. The snip the compendium previously used is aphorism IV ('tell me what kind of food you eat...'), which says nothing on variation.

ourUse: variation.js: detect a prose piece's redundant opening (first 8 words; sameOpening = 4+ shared leading words), first rewrite it mechanically (snipVariation: synonym swap or rotation, no model), and only if that fails run variedDraw: draw at rising temperature and reject any output whose opening still matches a blocked construction. Handle comment: 'flavor is measure, the chosen accent, never a dump.'

bends.ours: Compendium: 'whose whole method is appetite varied and sampled. Varied draws, tried and kept or rejected, a tasting.'
bends.theirs: The book has no method of drawing and rejecting variants; it is aphorism, essay and anecdote on food, digestion and hospitality. Rejection sampling is our device.

bends.ours: The organ and its snip carry aphorism IV (you are what you eat); no manifest tied the handle to variation until aphorism XIII was added here.
bends.theirs: IV is about character revealed by diet; it does not support variation. XIII (change your drinks; the tongue saturates) is the one real hook.

bends.ours: Repeated sentence openings in prose treated as 'boring redundancy' to vary.
bends.theirs: XIII is about sensory saturation of the palate when a drink is repeated; applying it to repeated prose openings is our analogy.

bends.ours: variation.js opens 'Brillat-Savarin speaks:' with IV, then generated text: 'This file implements the teachings of Brillat-Savarin... I believe that the focus on the human experience of eating should be prioritized over a purely technical understanding.'
bends.theirs: He wrote none of that, and the file implements a prose-variation algorithm, not his teachings; the first-person sentence is model-written under his name.

bends.ours: Header: 'flavor is measure, the chosen accent, never a dump', after the gastronome.
bends.theirs: I found no such sentence in the text (searched 'accent', 'measure'); the one 'accent' hits are unrelated. It is our phrase.

fix: compendium work: 'Brillat-Savarin, in the Physiology of Taste, held that varying what one drinks matters because the tongue saturates on repetition (aphorism XIII). Our variation.js borrows only that idea of avoiding repetition; the snip-then-rejection-sampling method is ours.'
